notes: The 1983 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: dedications, the Central City Park ground-breaking, and plans for the South of Market park and Twin Peaks.

coverage.remaining: Routine items not curated. Not placed: South Drive renamed Martin Luther King, Jr. Drive (Dec 15, Res. 13497; no place page), Great Highway redesign (Michael Painter), a proposed Chinatown park on Powell Street, zoo pump station and koala exhibit.
coverage.note: Dated by footers. Curated list F1983.py.

findings.description: Officer John S. Macaulay Park, the mini park at the northeast corner of Larkin and O'Farrell Streets bought and developed under the Open Space Program, was to be dedicated on February 22, 1983, with Mayor Dianne Feinstein and Police Chief Con Murphy; the general manager reported it well designed and well lighted.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, February 10, 1983

resolution.method: A named park, playground or park building placed on its Recreation and Park place page by the name and streets the minutes give.

findings.description: With the first-phase contract to clear the Downtown Bowl site let, and the final plans by Royston, Hanamoto, Alley & Abey near completion after extensive community participation and help from the Police Department, a ground-breaking celebration for Central City Park was held at Eddy and Jones Streets on March 11, 1983, with Mayor Dianne Feinstein.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, March 10, 1983

findings.description: The Biblical Garden walk in the arboretum, renovated with a $14,000 gift from the Sisterhood Guild of Congregation Emanu-El, which also funded a City College student intern, was to be rededicated on June 2, 1983.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, May 19, 1983

findings.description: The general manager reported that the community had approved Omi Lang Associates' schematic plans for the new Open Space park at 6th and Folsom Streets, balancing green park with children's play apparatus and a multi-use athletic court, and that an architect had been chosen to renovate the large building on the property.

findings.description: Keith Kawamura of Michael Painter Associates presented to the Recreation and Park Commission a plan to upgrade Christmas Tree Point, Twin Peaks' main view area, with three vista areas, seating, directory maps and telescopes.
